Subject: SummaHealth: follow-up on PII handling for prompts & output logs

Hey Elena — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can close out the technical qualification items for procurement:

- What we captured today: Summa will send free-form clinical notes and patient identifiers in prompts for the triage assistant POC.
- Questions from your security team we want to confirm: what parts of the prompt/response are stored, where they’re stored, retention windows, and access/logging controls (who can see debug logs).
- Next steps from us: attach a concise matrix with current defaults and configurable knobs. Can you confirm if you need a version that keeps outputs ephemeral for the POC (no persisted outputs) or if you prefer short-term retention so you can run QA?

I attached a short matrix (summa-data-handling-matrix.xlsx) and a one-page summary of Redwood defaults. High-level answers below; we’ll hand off the more detailed cryptography and logging answers to Karthik and Neha.

High-level (POC):
- Prompt inputs: transmitted over TLS. By default in hosted mode we retain request metadata and full payloads for 30 days for debugging; this is configurable.
- Generated outputs: can be configured to be ephemeral (no write to persistent object storage) for the POC, or retained for a configurable TTL. Default short-term retention is 30 days.
- Logging/debug traces: limited debug logs (request id, routing, model variant) are retained 90 days by default; full-text debug capture that includes prompt/response payloads is off by default and requires explicit enablement and elevated access controls.
- Region: data-at-rest location can be pinned to US or EU regions for Dedicated/Private deployments. Hosted API defaults to region-based storage depending on customer tenancy.

If that aligns, I’ll loop in Karthik for the encryption/PKI and Neha for logging access controls. Prefer to get this confirmed this week so procurement can move to redlines.

Thanks,

Hi Elena — answers below, kept intentionally concise for the RFP. Happy to expand or sign an addendum if you need.

- Encryption:
  - In transit: TLS 1.2+ (mutual TLS available for Dedicated/Private).
  - At rest: AES-256 for object storage and database volumes. Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted accounts can use Redwood-managed KMS or bring-your-own (BYOK) for an enterprise plan.

- Prompt & output retention (configurable tenancy settings):
  - POC profile (per Summa request): prompt inputs TTL = 7 days, outputs = ephemeral (no object-store write). We will tag and exclude ephemeral payloads from backups.
  - Production defaults: prompt inputs = 90 days, outputs = 90 days (configurable down to 0). We can set custom TTLs per route.

- Debug capture & RBAC:
  - Full-text debug capture is OFF by default. If enabled, access is governed by RBAC tied to Redwood SSO groups. We require an allowlist for customer-designated external users.
  - Role examples: Support-Read (exposes metadata only), Debug-Read (exposes full payload), Admin (full access).
  - Access requests: submitted through our Console with audit trail; approvals require Security or Legal sign-off for external customers.

- Audit logs / SIEM export:
  - Audit events: read/write/access events, admin actions, API keys changes. Format: JSON lines (timestamp, actor, action, resource, request_id).
  - Retention: default 365 days for accounts on enterprise plan; configurable. For POC we can provide 90-day retention or stream events to your Splunk instance in near-real-time (syslog over TLS or S3 push).

- Residency & Deployment:
  - Hosted: tenancy region controls object storage region; we can pin storage to US regions for SummaHealth.
  - Dedicated/Private: fully US-only deployment possible (VPC, private control plane, on-prem option).

- Evidence / certifications:
  - We can provide SOC 2 Type II report excerpts and encryption attestations under NDA.

Attachments I’m including: redwood-prompt-data-summary.pdf (short defaults) and the updated summa-data-handling-matrix.xlsx with the POC TTLs pre-filled.

If that covers it, Vanessa, please bundle into the RFP response and I’ll prepare a short statement for the security appendix.
